prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1259; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the northbound lane on a city street in Pasadena, Texas, when a vehicle operated by Driver 2 crossed into the same lane and the two front ends made contact at low speed. Driver 1 reported pain in the right wrist after the impact and was transported for evaluation. The wrist complaint is consistent with the force and direction of the collision as observed at the scene. Both vehicles sustained front-end damage that corresponds closely to the impact described by each driver, and scene photographs document this damage. No prior damage to the vehicle operated by Driver 1 was identified during the inspection. Responding officers and the on-scene statements confirm that a passenger was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision. No independent witnesses came forward, so the account relies on the drivers' statements and the physical evidence. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
